newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shiseido's earnings soar on overseas expansion.
newsitem.headline: Shiseido's earnings soar on overseas expansion.

text.p: Aggressive expansion abroad and a pick-up in sales of cosmetics at home lifted Shiseido Co Ltd's earnings to record highs in the past business year, the company said on Tuesday.

"In the first year of our five-year globalisation plan, we worked hard to improve our business both abroad and in Japan," a Shiseido official said. "Our group and parent profits and sales hit record highs, which means business is doing great."

Japan's largest cosmetics firm said that its parent current profit rose five percent to 32.46 billion yen ($272 million) in the year to end-March 1997, while group profits jumped 16 percent to 40.98 billion yen ($344 million)
Current profit is pre-tax profit including gains and losses on non-operating activities such as securities investments.

"Parent results were as expected but group earnings were very healthy," said Keiko Sasaki, an analyst at ING Barings. "Business abroad is growing steadily and in Japan the firm has diversified its products, which has proved quite successful."

Shiseido, which enjoys a near 20 percent share of Japan's 1.43 trillion yen ($12.0 billion) cosmetics market, unveiled plans to boost overseas sales to 200 billion yen ($1.68 billion) by 2000 from 50.4 billion yen ($423 million) in 1995.

Overseas sales, which accounted for 11 percent of Shiseido's group sales, rose 28 percent in 1996/97 thanks to its expansion into emerging markets such as Brazil, Turkey, Israel, Cyprus and the Czech Republic, it said.
Analysts said that Shiseido's biggest test will be in Asia, with its fast developing economies. The firm already has plans to add Vietnam to its customer list in September.

"The firm has rational expansion plans, aiming to capture Asia with its products, sell perfumes and luxury cosmetics in Europe and strengthen manufacturing bases in the United States by buying facilities such as those of Carter-Wallace Inc," said Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd analyst Kumi Miyauchi.
This year, group profits are forecast at 43 billion yen ($361 million), helped partly by its growing overseas business.

Domestically, Shiseido said sales of skin care products for middle-aged women helped profits. The purchase of Helene Curtis Industries Inc's Japanese units from Unilever NV, which makes Shiseido a major player in Japan's beauty salon business, is expected to contribute to earnings in the future.

"The domestic cosmetics market is mature, with annual growth of about two percent," said Kazuhisa Sugita, an analyst at Lehman Brothers Japan Inc. "The only way for Shiseido to grow is to go abroad and so far, it seems to be living up to its plans." ($1=119 yen)
